statement: Apply the strict budget (11.5) on the geometric generic field of Kw over the independent probes g, choosing the optional Ūj to include generators of the relative field. Assume each probe has a fixed angular lift gj = Gj with Gj ∈ Vdj . Any prescribed shift is assumed to satisfy the Taylor leading-term hypothesis of Lemma 12.4 and to have an expansion in fixed homogeneous factors with angular lifts and bounded factor counts divided by P0. Clear all the rational exponents by one positive integer kI. The trace product may be chosen so that the multiplicities of the active factors in its lift H are (12.5) (P0 − 1)τiαi, τi ≥ 0, X i τi = 1 or X i τi ≤ 1 if the cap is active. 76 OPENAI The multiplicity of a tiny factor Ūj is at most (P0 − 1)ej. Expanding the Taylor flags adds between zero and P0 − 1 copies of each probe. Every surviving homogeneous initial summand has an actual traced output F′ of degree at most its total physical input degree divided by P0, plus n. At the chosen w its value satisfies equality in (12.3); on a local affine continuation in the same open stratum cone the lower inequality remains available. Common mandatory factors included in every generator of the input system remain in every product and every expanded summand. All output spaces and finite cutoff comparisons needed for this conclusion may be chosen before p and P0, from bounds for the normalized factor counts.
